subject: Apportionment guidelines for divisional invoice credits
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Greene <sarah.greene@acme-health.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Apportionment guidelines for divisional invoice credits

Hi Sarah,

Thanks again for the call this morning. To make the upcoming credit memos and invoice adjustments straightforward for both sides, we wanted to propose a consistent apportionment approach across Acme's legal entities. From our side we can support either:

- Pro rata by numeric invoice lines (net value share per line)
- Allocation by cost center tag (you supply cost-center mapping)
- Per-seat / per-license split (if licenses are assigned by entity)

Could you confirm which method you prefer? Also useful for our billing flow: whether Acme prefers a single master credit memo with internal apportionment entries, or separate credit memos issued per Acme entity.

For VAT/tax treatment we need to know the billing entity for each portion (Acme US vs Acme EU) and whether you want us to net VAT on issuance or let you run a reverse-charge. I attached a short draft (proposal-apportionment-draft.pdf) that outlines the options and a sample output.

If you prefer, we can prepare a sample credit memo showing the split across two entities and the accompanying GL mapping for your accounting team.

Next steps I suggest: you confirm preferred apportionment method and the legal entities to map; we'll produce a sample credit memo + intercompany draft for review.

Thanks,
--
Karthik Iyer
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0186

Attachment: proposal-apportionment-draft.pdf (PDF, 98KB)

From: Sarah Greene <sarah.greene@acme-health.com>

Subject: Re: Apportionment guidelines for divisional invoice credits

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the clear options. We would prefer pro rata by net-line value for this engagement — that will map best to our internal cost owners. For VAT, for the EU portion we'd expect reverse charge to be applied where appropriate; our tax team will confirm which lines are subject.

Please go ahead and send the sample credit memo and the matrix so our accounting team can validate GL codes. Also include any recommended memo wording that helps our AP process the intercompany adjustments.

I'll loop billing@acme-health.com here in case they need the attachments in a separate thread.

Best,
Sarah

Can you confirm the following so we can produce everything in one pass:
1) GL mapping: if you want us to use a specific GL per cost center, send the mapping; otherwise we'll propose standard GLs (revenue adjustment, contra-revenue, intercompany receivable/payable).
2) VAT approach: confirm if Acme would prefer reverse-charge on EU lines or if you want Redwood to re-invoice with VAT included for the EU entity.
3) Splits by currency: if any lines are in EUR, should we invoice the EU entity in EUR or keep master in USD and post fx internally?

I've attached a working matrix (apportionment-matrix.xlsx) to show the format we'd use — it includes columns for line value, pro-rata factor, target entity, and suggested GL code.

If you want a staged approach we can: (A) issue a master credit + intercompany routing; (B) issue separate entity-level credits. Our preference for transaction transparency is (A) where we issue a master and create internal AP/AR moves so you see one customer-facing document.

Thanks — let me know if you want me to draft the credit memo sample for review.

--
Karthik Iyer
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Attachment: apportionment-matrix.xlsx (Excel, 24KB)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Greene <sarah.greene@acme-health.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-22T10:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Apportionment guidelines for divisional invoice credits — proposed execution

Hi all,

Thanks Karthik — looping in billing ops notes and next steps. Based on Sarah's preference for pro rata by net-line value and the VAT guidance, here is a recommended execution plan we can implement immediately: 

1) Customer-facing document: issue one master credit memo to Acme Health (single customer-facing transaction) showing total credit amount and an appendix that lists the apportioned amounts per entity. That appendix will be the auditable artifact for your AP. (See attached credit-memo-stub.pdf)

2) Internal accounting: Redwood will post internal intercompany entries to move the apportioned amounts to the designated Acme legal entities. We will generate intercompany invoices/credit notes for your consolidation. See intercompany-routing-instructions.docx for the default GLs we plan to use (contra-revenue / intercompany receivable / intercompany payable).

3) VAT treatment: for EU-entity portions we will mark lines for reverse-charge where your tax team indicates; if reverse charge is not applicable we can reissue entity-level invoices with VAT included — flag those lines now and we'll handle reissuance.

4) Currency: we will invoice the master in USD by default and post intercompany moves in local currencies if required. If you need the EU entity invoiced in EUR please confirm and provide the FX date (billing date or agreed conversion date).

Action items for Acme:
- Confirm GL codes for each cost center column in the attached matrix (column 'Target GL')
- Confirm whether reverse-charge applies to all EU lines or only a subset
- Provide AP contact and any required billing reference (PO# / billing code)

Once we have your confirmations we'll produce: 1) final credit memo PDF for signature, 2) intercompany invoice set, 3) journal entry file for your ERP import. Expect the draft packages within 48 business hours of confirmation.

Marissa (cc Rishi) — can you confirm the GL code set we plan to use and whether we need additional supporting docs for tax/vat audit?

Thanks,
--
Marissa Cole
Finance Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
